items.description: Permanent fix, as one action: a Jenkins pipeline that takes a deploy repo. One `IaC/Destroy Stage` build, given a deploy repo and a stage, permanently deletes what that retired stage left: its Terraform resources, its state in TerraformState and its `config/<stage>/`. No other step is needed. That holds whatever the stage's state holds: the namespaced Kubernetes objects in it, already gone with the pruned namespace, are dropped from state rather than deleted (Ruling review r1 F1, V20).
items.rationale: One build chains guard, Job (plan, destroy, state removal) and config removal; the live dry run exercised everything up to the write; the apply itself is V10.

items.description: The guard fails the build before any Job starts if ArgoCDDeploy's registry on `main` (`releases/values.yaml`; e.g. `fieldnotes` → `https://github.com/pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy.git` with stage `prd`, `releases/values.yaml:99-102`) has an entry deploying REPO's STAGE, or if a live Application in `argocd-prd` sources REPO with Helm parameter `hook.stage` = STAGE. Single-source and multi-source (`spec.sources[]`) Applications both count. The failure names what still deploys the stage. There is no namespace check.
items.rationale: Live: prd dry run failed in 'Check stage is undeployed' before any Job, naming both registry entry and live Application. Code matches single- and multi-source and has no namespace check.
evidence: IaC/Destroy Stage #3 FAILURE: 'prd of pvginkel/FieldnotesDeploy is still deployed, by the registry entry apps.fieldnotes.stages.prd ... and the live Application argocd-prd/fieldnotes-prd'

items.area: R2.2 the Job and the empty configuration
items.description: The pipeline runs the argocd-hook image as a one-off Job in `argocd-hooks`, with the `tf-presync` ServiceAccount and the `argocd-hook-credentials` Secret, under a name no `tf-presync-<namespace>` sync Job can take (`/work/Charts/charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:38`). Its destroy mode clones the deploy repo at a SHA, starts the state backend and inits against `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/terraform.tfstate` (`argocd-hook/presync/backend.py:52-54`). It sets the stage's namespaced Kubernetes objects aside (V20) and plans against a configuration that holds only the root's provider, backend and variable declarations. It passes the stage's tfvars when `config/<stage>/` exists (Ruling review r1 A2). So every other resource in state is an orphan planned for deletion, and `prevent_destroy` no longer binds. A repo whose declarations do not init or plan this way fails the build loudly.
items.rationale: Job destroy-stage-2 ran in argocd-hooks as tf-presync with argocd-hook-credentials, cloned, inited against the dev state, planned against the empty configuration and showed the two orphans as destroyed.
evidence: IaC/Destroy Stage #2 log: 'module.data.homelab_rbd_image.this will be destroyed (because ... is not in configuration)'
argocd-hook tests green in sweep r2

items.description: With `APPLY=true` the Job destroys from the plan it saved, checks that the state lists no resources, and then `git rm`s `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/` from TerraformState, using the hook's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
items.rationale: Not run live (APPLY=true is operator-gated). Read destroy.py and test_destroy.py, which the green sweep ran: destroy from saved plan, empty-state check, removal of argocd/<repo>/<stage>/ with GITHUB_TOKEN.

items.description: With `APPLY=true`, once the Job has succeeded, Jenkins commits `git rm -r config/<stage>` to the deploy repo's `main` with the GitHub credential it uses for version pins (JenkinsPipelineUtils `vars/cicd.groovy:66`).
items.rationale: Read: 'Remove config folder' stage runs after the Job, only when APPLY, git rm -r config/<stage>, push to main with credential 5f6fbd66 (the version-pin credential). Not run live; the live run belongs to V10.

items.description: Each part lands where R2 and Ruling D1 put it: the destroy mode and `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` in ArgoCDTools, the grants in ArgoCDDeploy, the dedicated ServiceAccount in JenkinsDeploy, the design as an argo-cd decision in AnsibleSpecs, and a section on the pipeline in this repo's argocd runbook.
items.rationale: Destroy mode and Jenkinsfile in ArgoCDTools, grants in ArgoCDDeploy, ServiceAccount in JenkinsDeploy, D66 in AnsibleSpecs argo-cd, runbook section in Ansible.

items.area: R3 APPLY and the dry run
items.description: An `APPLY` parameter; `APPLY=false` is a dry run. `APPLY` defaults to false. A dry run plans and stops: it shows the destroy plan, lists separately the namespaced Kubernetes objects an apply would forget (Ruling review r1 F1), and names the state file and `config/<stage>/` it would delete. It changes nothing: no resource, no state write, no TerraformState commit, no deploy-repo commit. `APPLY=true` plans and destroys inside the same Job, from the saved plan, with no `input` step.
items.rationale: Dry run #2: plan shown, apply stages skipped by `when`, 'an apply removes argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/ from the state repository', 'dry run: nothing was written', 'An apply removes config/dev/ ... pushed nothing'. APPLY defaults false. TerraformState dev state and FieldnotesDeploy config/dev still present afterwards.
evidence: gh api: TerraformState argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev has terraform.tfstate; FieldnotesDeploy config/dev has terraform.tfvars; FieldnotesDeploy main unchanged at 14ec1f7

items.area: R4 / Ruling D3 dev dry run
items.description: FieldnotesDeploy `dev` is the first stage it destroys. The test phase starts `IaC/Destroy Stage` with `APPLY=false` against FieldnotesDeploy `dev`. The plan shows exactly the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data` and the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` for deletion, and the build lists nothing as forgotten. The build names `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` (TerraformState holds `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/terraform.tfstate`, 8120 bytes, at `1b32f10`) and `config/dev/` as what an apply would delete. Afterwards, both are still present.
items.rationale: Dry run plans exactly 2 to destroy: module.data.homelab_rbd_image.this (fieldnotes-dev-data) and the PV fieldnotes-dev-data-pv. The state holds no namespaced object, so nothing is listed as forgotten ('nothing to forget'). Names the state folder and config/dev/. Both still present afterwards.
evidence: IaC/Destroy Stage #2: 'Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 2 to destroy.'
log: 'the state holds no namespaced Kubernetes object: nothing to forget'

items.description: The test phase starts `IaC/Destroy Stage` once with `APPLY=false` against FieldnotesDeploy `prd`, and the guard fails the build. The registry entry `fieldnotes`/`prd` and the live `fieldnotes-prd` Application, whose `hook.stage` is `prd`, both still deploy that stage.
items.rationale: The prd dry run failed in the guard naming both the registry entry and the live Application.

items.description: The operator's `APPLY=true` build against FieldnotesDeploy `dev` leaves the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data`, the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` and `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` in TerraformState gone, and `config/dev/` deleted from FieldnotesDeploy (ANS-147's done-when).
items.owed_after: the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against FieldnotesDeploy dev (Ruling D3)
items.rationale: Operator's APPLY=true build is the settling run (close-out A1).
evidence: Operator runs IaC/Destroy Stage with REPO=FieldnotesDeploy STAGE=dev APPLY=true

items.description: A new argo-cd decision records the Destroy Stage design and supersedes D28 (`argo-cd/decisions.md:382`), which carries the supersession marker. It carries the narrow overrule of D1 and D33/D41 for this operator-started pipeline only. No existing entry (D1, D27 as amended, D31, D33, D39, D41) is left contradicting it.
items.rationale: D66 exists, D28 carries the Superseded marker, D1/D27/D31/D33/D39/D41 carry Amended or D66-citing notes.

items.description: The pipeline's cluster work runs as a dedicated ServiceAccount in `jenkins-prd`. It is defined in JenkinsDeploy and named by `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage`'s pod spec. It is bound to a Role in `argocd-hooks` that holds only what the pipeline's Job lifecycle uses, and to a read-only Role on `argoproj.io` Applications in `argocd-prd`. The shared agent ServiceAccount `jenkins-prd/default` (JenkinsDeploy `chart/templates/jenkins-agent-jobs-rolebinding.yaml:9`) gains nothing. ArgoCDDeploy's render gate pins both grants.
items.rationale: Live: Role destroy-stage in argocd-hooks (jobs get/create/delete, pods get/list, pods/log get) and in argocd-prd (applications get/list), both bound to jenkins-prd/destroy-stage only; jenkins-agent-jobs still binds only default. Build runs as serviceAccount destroy-stage. Render gate green.
evidence: kubectl get role/rolebinding in argocd-hooks, argocd-prd, jenkins-prd
ArgoCDDeploy tests green in sweep r2

items.description: The dedicated ServiceAccount and both of its grants are live on prd before the test phase's dry runs. JenkinsDeploy's `jenkins-prd` Application auto-syncs (live `syncPolicy.automated`). ArgoCDDeploy's chart reaches prd only through a sync of `argocd-prd`, which is not auto-synced (`releases/values.yaml:30`, `autoSync: false`). The test phase syncs `argocd-prd` itself, once, through the elevated `~/.kube/config-prd-write`, and only after a diff of `argocd-prd`'s live state against the pushed ArgoCDDeploy revision shows nothing but this slice's Roles and RoleBindings (on 2026-10-02 `argocd-prd` was `Synced` at `9334541`, ArgoCDDeploy's `origin/main`). If anything else differs it does not sync, and this criterion, V08 and V09 are left owed to the operator.
items.rationale: SA live via JenkinsDeploy auto-sync. Before syncing, argocd-prd listed exactly four OutOfSync resources: the destroy-stage Roles and RoleBindings in argocd-hooks and argocd-prd (the redis-secret-init rows are Argo hooks). I synced those four resources only, at b8d1a0c, through config-prd-write, which also keeps the PreSync hook from running. Result Synced / Succeeded.
evidence: kubectl get application argocd-prd: Synced Succeeded 'successfully synced (all tasks run)'

items.description: The destroy mode is a separate entry point of the hook image. The sync hook's four-positional contract (`argocd-hook/presync/cli.py:16-26`), `tests/test_cli.py`'s `ArgumentContractTests`, the Charts render gate and the Charts `hook.imageTag` pin (`"10"`, `charts/homelab-shared/values.yaml:7`) are all unchanged. The pipeline runs `registry:5000/argocd-hook:latest`.
items.rationale: cli.py and tests/test_cli.py are not in the ArgoCDTools diff; Charts imageTag stays "10"; the Job runs registry:5000/argocd-hook:latest (IaC/ArgoCDTools #27 at fa32363 pushed it).

items.description: Re-runs are idempotent. An already-empty state skips the destroy, and a state file or `config/<stage>/` folder that is already gone is skipped. Without `config/<stage>/` the Job still reaches its state checks (Ruling review r1 A2), although the sync's own helper refuses such a clone (`argocd-hook/presync/terraform.py:35-37`). A run against a stage with no state file creates none, and a build that stopped halfway is finished by running it again. The hook's unittest suite covers the dry run, the apply, the re-runs, a clone without `config/<stage>/` and an empty configuration that does not plan.
items.rationale: Code and unit tests cover the re-runs (sweep r2 argocd-hook test GREEN); not exercised live (APPLY=false only).

items.description: The repository webhook goes with the stage whose state manages it (`manage_webhook`, argo-cd D39). FieldnotesDeploy `dev` does not manage it (`config/dev/terraform.tfvars:4`, `manage_webhook = false`), so its plan shows no webhook.
items.rationale: The dev dry-run plan shows no webhook resource, only the RBD image and the PV.

items.description: The job `IaC/Destroy Stage` exists in the `IaC/` folder, created through the Jenkins API to the style guide (Ruling review r1 A1). Its configuration holds only the job, its SCM and its Script Path (JenkinsPipelineUtils `docs/pages/guide/job-properties.md:3-5`). Its parameters come from `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` through one parameter-less registration build, and so do its lack of triggers and its refusal of concurrent builds. That build fails on the empty `REPO` before any cluster call and changes nothing. Once registered, the job has no triggers, allows no concurrent builds, and defaults `APPLY` to false. The run starts no build of it except that registration build and Ruling D3's two dry runs.
items.rationale: Job exists in IaC/ with config.xml holding only the job, SCM and Script Path, no triggers. Registration build #1 failed on the empty REPO before any cluster call and registered REPO, STAGE, APPLY (default false) and disableConcurrentBuilds; concurrentBuild is false. Only builds: #1 registration, #2/#3 dry runs.

items.description: `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage` follows the estate's Jenkins pipeline style guide (https://pipelines.home/docs/).
items.rationale: Read against the style guide: declarative, library by identifier, podYaml, serviceAccount, disableConcurrentBuilds with the reason, timeout, timestamps, credentials in withCredentials with set +x, notify.error on abort. Ran twice cleanly.

items.description: This repo's argocd runbook has a section on destroying a retired stage with the pipeline: when it applies (after undeploy), the dry run first, then the apply, what the guard refuses, and re-running. The undeploy paragraph no longer says that nothing prunes the state (`docs/runbooks/argocd.md:387`).
items.rationale: Runbook section at docs/runbooks/argocd.md:395-465 covers the dry run, the apply, the guard and re-running; the undeploy paragraph no longer says nothing prunes state.

items.area: Ruling review r1 F1 namespaced objects
items.description: Before planning, the destroy mode drops every Kubernetes object in the stage's state that lives in a namespace from state, without deleting it. Such an object went with the namespace when the Application was pruned, and the Job's identity has no grant left on it. Its only namespaced grant, `tf-presync-app` on Secrets, is bound in the app's own namespace alone (ArgoCDDeploy `chart/templates/hook-namespace.yaml:106-125`, Charts `charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:42-59`). Cluster-scoped objects such as PVs stay in the plan and are destroyed for real, and so is everything outside Kubernetes: databases, buckets, RBD images. A dry run lists the forgotten objects separately, as already gone with the namespace, and still writes nothing. An apply forgets them and destroys the rest. `tf-presync` gains no grant. The hook's unittest suite covers a state that holds a namespaced Secret beside a PV and a resource outside Kubernetes.
items.rationale: The dev dry run reported 'nothing to forget', so the live path with namespaced objects was not exercised. Code and unit tests (a namespaced Secret beside a PV and a non-Kubernetes resource) are in the green sweep; T2 covers the one gap.
